articles.title: The SCARE Score: A Simplified Risk Score for Predicting Intraoperative Neuromonitoring Signal Loss in Pediatric Spinal Deformity Surgery.
articles.authors: Moore DM, Keohane D, Haffey S, Noel J, Kiely P, O'Kelly P, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
articles.sample_size: 413 spinal deformity surgeries in 360 patients between 2020 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Intraoperative neuromonitoring signal loss during surgery; development and validation of the SCARE risk prediction score
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a simple scoring system called SCARE that helps surgeons identify children at higher risk of losing nerve monitoring signals during spinal deformity surgery. The score considers spinal cord shape, the severity of the deformity, whether it is revision surgery, and whether the child has a genetic syndrome, helping surgeons plan safer operations and prepare families for what to expect.

articles.title: Three-Year Outcomes Following Hip Reconstruction in Cerebral Palsy: A Population-Based Analysis.
articles.authors: Golzar A, Hamad CD, Wiener J, Liu T, Dajani AJ, Kaelber DC, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national healthcare database
articles.population: Children and young adults aged 1 to 25 years with cerebral palsy who had hip reconstruction surgery
articles.outcomes: Hardware removal, hip dislocation, infection, and mortality measured up to 3 years after surgery
articles.take_home: About 4 in 10 children needed hardware removal or experienced hip dislocation within 3 years of hip reconstruction surgery. Most hip dislocations happened in the first year, but most hardware removals and infections occurred later, suggesting that long-term monitoring after surgery may be important.

articles.title: Proximal junctional kyphosis in distraction-based growth-friendly treatment: Definition, risk factors, and timeline.
articles.authors: Beydemir A, Ramazanov R, Berktas M, Ayvaz M, Demirkiran HG, Yazici M
articles.population: Children with early-onset scoliosis treated with dual-rod distraction-based growth-friendly systems
articles.outcomes: Development of proximal junctional kyphosis (abnormal bending at the top of the treated spine), timing of onset, and risk factors
articles.take_home: Proximal junctional kyphosis developed in about 1 in 5 patients, usually after the first year following surgery. The main risk factors were having significant pre-operative thoracic kyphosis and selecting certain vertebrae as the top of the instrumentation.

articles.title: Utility of the Modified Clavien-Dindo-Sink (mCDS) Grading System for Classifying Casting Complication Severity in Early Onset Scoliosis Patients.
articles.authors: Stern E, Kappler E, Hart M, Anari JB, Garg S, Li Y
articles.population: Children aged 10 years or younger undergoing serial casting for early-onset scoliosis
articles.outcomes: Complications classified using modified Clavien-Dindo-Sink grading system; 15.6% of patients had at least one complication
articles.take_home: Most casting complications were minor (grades II and IIIb), with the most common serious complication being need for early cast removal and re-application. The current grading system may overstate casting risks compared to surgical risks, and modifications to the system are needed for better comparison.

articles.title: The Swedish experience of capital realignment surgery for slipped capital femoral epiphysis: results from a nationwide retrospective cohort of 28 patients.
articles.authors: Nilsson J, Lindell M, Ortegren J, Herngren B, Stenmarker M, Michno P, et al.
articles.population: Patients with slipped capital femoral epiphysis treated with capital realignment surgery
articles.outcomes: Avascular necrosis of the femoral head (primary outcome); patient-reported hip and groin symptoms using HAGOS and iHOT12 scores (clinical outcomes)
articles.take_home: Capital realignment surgery for slipped capital femoral epiphysis resulted in avascular necrosis in 22% of patients, though none of the cases where blood supply to the femoral head was monitored during surgery developed this complication. Patient outcomes were better when surgery was performed as the first treatment within a month of diagnosis.

articles.title: Back Pain in Adolescents and Young Adults: A Retrospective Review of Psychosocial Factors and Treatment Strategies.
articles.authors: Richard HM, Shobode MA, Murata A, Franko G, Mansour A, Owusu-Ansah M, et al.
articles.population: Children and young adults aged 7 to 22 years presenting with back pain to paediatric orthopaedic and sports medicine clinics
articles.outcomes: Persistent back pain symptoms at follow-up; structural spine diagnoses; behavioural health diagnoses; pain severity
articles.take_home: In young people with back pain, behavioural health problems like depression and ADHD were more strongly linked to ongoing pain than structural spine problems such as spondylolysis or scoliosis. Assessing and treating mental health alongside physical treatment may help reduce persistent back pain in this age group.

articles.title: Frailty and Surgical Invasiveness Are Independently Associated with Complications in Pediatric Spinal Deformity Surgery.
articles.authors: Chan V, Simmonds A, Maclean L, Parsons D, Vitale MG, Skaggs DL
articles.population: Children undergoing spinal fusion for spinal deformity
articles.outcomes: Any adverse event, severe adverse event, unplanned reoperation, and unplanned readmission within 30 days after surgery
articles.take_home: Children who are frail or having more complex spinal surgery have higher rates of complications after surgery. The risk is highest when both frailty and surgical complexity are present, which should help doctors and families plan care and discuss realistic expectations before surgery.

articles.title: Children With Synpolydactyly Type I Homozygous HOXD13 Mutations: Embryology and Surgical Correction of the "Cupping" of the Hands and Feet.
articles.authors: Alsayegh SO, Alghamdi AM, Al-Qattan MM
articles.population: Children with familial Synpolydactyly Type I homozygous HOXD13 mutations
articles.outcomes: Partial correction of cupping deformity; improved foot positioning and hand function; parental satisfaction
articles.take_home: Surgery can partially correct severe hand and foot deformities in children with this genetic condition, with good functional results and parental satisfaction at follow-up of more than 5 years.

articles.title: Palliative hip surgery in nonambulatory children with cerebral palsy: outcomes of two surgical techniques.
articles.authors: Lodovici V, Marre Brunenghi G, Marengo L, Maltinti M, Parchi PD, Canavese F
articles.population: Nonambulatory children with cerebral palsy (GMFCS V)
articles.outcomes: Pain relief, quality of life (caregiver-reported), hip joint migration, complications
articles.take_home: Both palliative hip surgery techniques provided good pain relief and improved quality of life for severely disabled children with cerebral palsy. One technique had fewer complications related to abnormal bone growth, though both had similar overall hip joint migration.
